validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, well-documented, currently active interstate gas transmission trunk. Confirmed independently via offshore-technology.com (GlobalData trade database profile of the system, calling it an active gas pipeline project) and a Jan. 2025 Federal Register notice (Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC blanket-authorization filing) showing ongoing FERC-regulated activity. The operator's own June-2026 'Phase IX' project brochure (energytransfer.com, PDF, verified 200 + manually confirmed via pdftotext since url_verifier's PDF text extraction missed the tokens) additionally shows the system still expanding (Phase IX targeted Q4 2028 in-service, 'more than 70 years of reliable service'), i.e. not a phantom, not retired. CLASSIFICATION: correctly a natural-gas transmission trunk (Fuel=Gas), not a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against the 45-row roster. P3242 (len 3.0 mi) and P4051 (len 24.7 mi), both also named 'Florida Gas Transmission Pipeline', are NOT duplicates of this network row -- the gem.wiki page itself lists named sub-projects (East-West Project, Galveston County Project, Putnam Expansion Project, East Louisiana Project, Big Bend Project), and a harvested Pipeline & Gas Journal 'Planned Projects' PDF (Oct. 2018, s3.amazonaws.com/pgj-wp-media, opened and read) independently confirms FGT files individual FERC projects like 'East-West Project' as separate line items distinct from the whole-system figure -- consistent with GGIT's convention of one network/system row (this one, spanning Port Lavaca, TX to Miami, FL) plus separate rows for discrete expansion-project segments. So P0190, P3242 and P4051 are legitimately distinct GEM entries, not a double count. Two real, separate spec problems found instead -- see the other validity entries on StartYear1 and Capacity.

validity.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 1998 to 1959 (original in-service year); 1998 is likely a mis-keyed FERC filing/expansion-phase date, not the pipeline's start year
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=1998 is materially wrong for a system-level start date. Two independent sources put the original in-service date at 1959: offshore-technology.com's GlobalData profile states outright 'The Florida Gas Transmission System project started operations in 1959,' and a Broward County Board of County Commissioners agenda exhibit ('History of Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC -- Pipeline License Agreement', cragenda.broward.org PDF, opened and read via pdftotext -- url_verifier flags a content-check FAIL on this PDF but that is the documented PDF-extraction limitation in url_verifier.py's own header; the 200 status is real and I manually confirmed the tokens '1967' and 'Florida Gas' are present in the extracted text) shows the County approving a pipeline license agreement with 'Florida Gas Transmission Company' as far back as October 17, 1967 -- i.e. the pipeline was already an established, operating system nearly 20 years before GEM's 1998 date. 1998 is most likely a mis-copied date from FGT's Phase IV expansion, which was filed with FERC on Dec. 1, 1998 (per Natural Gas Intelligence coverage found in search) -- a real event, but an expansion-phase filing date, not the system's start year. This is a spec error the whole way GEM's data-entry pattern for legacy 1950s-60s US interstate trunks (built well before FERC's modern e-Library) seems prone to: a later, easily-searchable expansion date gets substituted for an original in-service year that requires digging into historical/legal records to find.

validity.recommendation: update Capacity from 1,059.44 MMcf/d to reflect the system's actual current mainline capacity (~3.2-3.7 Bcf/d per independent sources); the current sheet value understates capacity by roughly 3x
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity=1,059.44 MMcf/d is materially too low for the current system. Rextag Corporation (independent commercial pipeline-GIS data vendor, unrelated to GEM, verified live) states FGT's current 'System Capacity: 3.7 Bcf/d' against 'Miles of Pipeline: 5380' for the same system. That figure is directionally consistent with FGT's own public expansion history: a 2009 Florida Public Service Commission filing (floridapsc.com, verified) discusses FGT having '139 MMcf/d of excess capacity that will be available following its Phase VIII expansion in 2011' -- i.e. total system capacity was already well above 1,059 MMcf/d even before the ~800 MMcf/d Phase VIII addition went in service, and the operator's own June-2026 Phase IX brochure describes a further planned expansion of 'up to 526 million cubic feet per day' on top of today's base, which would be nonsensical language for a system whose base capacity were only ~1,059 MMcf/d. I could not pin an exact independently-sourced Bcf/d figure to a specific year matching GEM's 1,059.44 precision, so I'm not proposing a replacement number to paste -- only flagging that the existing figure is stale/wrong and should be re-researched against a current FERC Index of Customers or FGT's own current tariff (Third Revised Volume No. 1) rather than being carried forward unchanged.

validity.researcher_notes: Operator/Owner1 = 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' 100% is the correct name of the direct FERC-jurisdictional operating/owning entity -- confirmed by Wikipedia ('FGT is owned by Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC, a 100 percent owned subsidiary of Citrus Corp') and independently by the Jan. 2025 Federal Register notice, which names 'Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC' as the filer/regulated entity.
